fit: chewing gum and measured swallowing events in Parkinson disease
assessment: The author abstract reports 3.10, 14.95 and 7.00 mean swallowing events before, during and after chewing gum. The sequential short-period study measures a proxy rather than graded drooling. It supplies no raw fig exposure.

fit: incident drooling under subthalamic stimulation and medical care
assessment: The adjusted stimulation hazard ratio was 1.4 with a 0.7 to 2.8 confidence interval. The cohort used an UPDRS threshold to define incident drooling without objective flow or dietary measures.

fit: corrected patient and caregiver survey severity categories
assessment: The corrigendum restores severity percentages for the original 382-response Parkinson's Europe survey. Its three reports reuse the same cohort. They measure perceived burden without an ingredient comparison.

fit: computational analysis of a food-derived peptide
assessment: The article examines a milk-derived candidate computationally and supplies no measured drooling or salivary-flow endpoint in vivo. No fig preparation or clinical direction.

fit: registered open-label prescription trial with separate drooling scales and flow measures
assessment: The first-session mean flow change was -0.34 g/min at week 4. The registered single-arm cohort includes several diagnoses, and only 24 entered session four. The clinical measurement and registry document one trial, without a fig comparator.

fit: drooling presence and plasma metabolites in Parkinson stage groups
assessment: Drooling was recorded in 11 of 20 intermediate-stage and 18 of 20 later-stage participants. It was a binary model input, with no severity change or fig exposure comparison.
